name: The Kachumbari Standoff
description: At a farewell nyama choma for Mr. Silas Onyango, departing for Canada, two attendees simultaneously claimed responsibility for the kachumbari. Each disputed the other's claim. A third attendee then stated she had also made kachumbari, producing a separate bowl from her bag. The original kachumbari's provenance has not been established. All three individuals are now in Canada.
prose: The farewell nyama choma gathering for Mr. Silas Onyango was held on 7 September 2019 at Njuguna's Place, Thika Road, Nairobi, fourteen days before Mr. Onyango's departure to Winnipeg, Canada, where he had secured a position in logistics. Twenty-two attendees were present. The meat was excellent. The incident occurred during the serving of accompaniments.

A bowl of kachumbari — finely diced tomato, onion, and coriander, dressed with lemon and chilli — was placed on the central table by an unspecified hand at approximately 4:30 PM. At 4:32 PM, Miss Tabitha Wambua stated to the table that she had made the kachumbari. At 4:33 PM, Mr. Geoffrey Odhiambo stated, with comparable confidence, that he had made the kachumbari. Both looked at the bowl. Both looked at each other.

A discussion followed lasting eleven minutes, during which Miss Wambua cited her use of the specific green chilli variety available at Ngong Road market and Mr. Odhiambo cited his distinctive lemon-to-onion ratio, which he described as his signature. Neither account could be verified from the bowl's contents alone, as the kachumbari had by this point been substantially consumed by attendees who had not been following the conversation.

At 4:44 PM, Mrs. Consolata Auma, seated at the far end of the table, reached into her tote bag and produced a second, larger bowl of kachumbari, which she placed beside the first. She stated that she had also made kachumbari and had been waiting for a gap in the conversation to bring it out. The conversation stopped. All three individuals emigrated to Canada within the following eighteen months. The provenance of the original bowl has not been established. The incident is OPEN.
heritageTrustNote: The Heritage Trust attempted to contact all three claimants via email in 2023. Miss Wambua responded to say she stood by her account. Mr. Odhiambo responded to say he also stood by his account and that he had since refined his lemon-to-onion ratio further. Mrs. Auma did not respond. The second bowl, by all accounts, was very good.

pullQuote.quote: She pulled it out of her bag. A full bowl. She had been sitting there with kachumbari in her bag the whole time, waiting.
pullQuote.attribution: Mr. Silas Onyango, 36, Guest of Honour, now of Winnipeg
